en: The Philippine eagle, our national bird, has a massive wingspan of up to two meters and is one of the world's largest and most powerful eagles.
Marcela Agoncillo and her daughter Lorenza hand-sewed the first Philippine flag in Hong Kong before bringing it back to the Philippines for the independence declaration.
The Philippine Senate has twenty-four members who serve six-year terms, with exactly half of the seats up for election every three years to maintain continuity.
The Ifugao people carved the Banaue Rice Terraces entirely by hand over two thousand years ago, creating a massive stairway to the clouds without modern machines.
Fe del Mundo became the first Asian woman admitted to Harvard Medical School and later invented a makeshift incubator using a bamboo basket and hot water bottles.
Before the Spanish arrived, most Filipinos could read and write Baybayin, an ancient alphabet carved into bamboo, leaves, and bark using sharp sticks and styluses.
During the Pahiyas Festival, Lucban residents decorate their house exteriors with kiping, which are vibrant, leaf-shaped wafers made from pounded rice and food coloring.
Jose Rizal was a brilliant polymath who could speak and write in twenty-two different languages, including Spanish, Latin, Greek, and several Asian dialects.
By law, the Philippine national flag must be flown upside down with the red stripe on top to signify a state of war.
The traditional bayanihan spirit was literally demonstrated when an entire community carried a heavy nipa hut on their shoulders to relocate it for a neighbor.
Filipino painter Juan Luna won a gold medal at the 1884 Madrid Exposition for his massive, dramatic masterpiece titled Spoliarium, bringing pride to the Philippines.
The Narra, our national tree, produces extremely hard and termite-resistant wood that is highly valued for building durable furniture and heavy structural beams.
